source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 6:13 = Song 7:1; public 7:1–13 = Song 7:2–14. All other labels match.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain superlative title and open Solomonic relation.
verses.before: The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.
verses.after: The Song of Songs, which belongs to Solomon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.

verses.rationale: Retain sudden third-to-second-person shift and bodily desire.
verses.before: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is better than wine.
verses.after: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! Your caresses are better than wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is better than wine.

verses.rationale: Keep name/oil image and young women’s attraction.
verses.before: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance; your name is oil poured out. So the young women love you.
verses.after: Your oils give off a lovely fragrance; your name is oil poured out. That is why the young women love you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance; your name is oil poured out. Therefore the maidens love you.

verses.rationale: Preserve singular/plural shifts without imposing one speaker scheme.
verses.before: Draw me after you; let us run. The king has brought me into his chambers. Let us rejoice and be glad in you; let us celebrate your love more than wine. Rightly do they love you.
verses.after: Draw me after you—let us run! The king has brought me into his rooms. We will rejoice and delight in you; we will celebrate your caresses more than wine. Rightly do they love you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Draw me after you; let us run. The king has brought me into his chambers. Let us rejoice and be glad in you; let us celebrate your love more than wine. Rightly do they love you.

verses.rationale: Render conjunction affirmatively and retain named comparisons.
verses.before: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
verses.after: I am black and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like Solomon’s curtains.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.

verses.rationale: Keep sun’s gaze, brothers’ coercion, and vineyard ambiguity.
verses.before: Do not stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has looked upon me. My mother's sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have not kept.
verses.after: Do not stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has gazed on me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me guard the vineyards. My own vineyard I did not guard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has looked upon me. My mother's sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have not kept.

verses.rationale: Preserve shepherd setting and veiled reading with note.
verses.before: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you pasture your flock? Where do you make it lie down at noon? Why should I be like one who wanders beside the flocks of your companions?
verses.after: Tell me, you whom my whole being loves, where you graze your flock, where you make it rest at noon. Why should I be like a veiled woman beside your companions’ flocks?
verses.tsw_comparator: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you pasture your flock? Where do you make it lie down at noon? Why should I be like one who wanders beside the flocks of your companions?

verses.rationale: Keep reply to female addressee and practical pastoral images.
verses.before: If you do not know, most beautiful among women, follow in the tracks of the flock, and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.
verses.after: If you do not know, most beautiful of women, follow the tracks of the flock and graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you do not know, most beautiful among women, follow in the tracks of the flock, and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.

verses.rationale: Retain surprising female horse and Pharaoh image.
verses.before: I compare you, my love, to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
verses.after: My love, I compare you to my mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: I compare you, my love, to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots.

verses.rationale: Keep adornment of cheeks and neck.
verses.before: Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.
verses.after: Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, your neck with strings of beads.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.

verses.rationale: Preserve plural makers and two metals.
verses.before: We will make for you ornaments of gold with studs of silver.
verses.after: We will make you ornaments of gold studded with silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: We will make for you ornaments of gold with studs of silver.

verses.rationale: Keep first-person fragrance and banquet setting.
verses.before: While the king was at his table, my perfume gave forth its fragrance.
verses.after: While the king was reclining at his table, my nard released its fragrance.
verses.tsw_comparator: While the king was at his table, my perfume gave forth its fragrance.

verses.rationale: Preserve intimate bodily perfume image.
verses.before: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh that lies between my breasts.
verses.after: My beloved is a pouch of myrrh to me, resting between my breasts.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh that lies between my breasts.

verses.rationale: Keep plant and specific place.
verses.before: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.
verses.after: My beloved is a cluster of henna blossoms to me in the vineyards of En-gedi.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated praise and direct dove metaphor.
verses.before: Look, you are beautiful, my love; look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves.
verses.after: How beautiful you are, my love! How beautiful! Your eyes are doves.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, you are beautiful, my love; behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves.

verses.rationale: Reflect masculine address and living bed image.
verses.before: Look, you are beautiful, my beloved, truly delightful. Our couch is luxuriant.
verses.after: How handsome you are, my beloved, how delightful! Our bed is green and flourishing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, truly delightful. Our couch is luxuriant.

verses.rationale: Retain architectural tree imagery and read-form rafters.
verses.before: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are cypresses.
verses.after: The beams of our houses are cedars; our rafters are cypresses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are cypresses.

verses.rationale: Avoid unsupported certainty of rose species; retain self-description.
verses.before: I am a flower of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
verses.after: I am a meadow flower of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am a flower of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

verses.rationale: Keep lover’s response and thorn contrast.
verses.before: Like a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
verses.after: Like a lily among thorns, so is my love among the young women.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

verses.rationale: Preserve sensory tree metaphor and male comparison.
verses.before: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the sons. In his shade I delighted to sit, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
verses.after: Like an apple tree among forest trees, so is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade; his fruit is sweet to my palate.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the sons. In his shade I delighted to sit, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.

verses.rationale: Keep wine house and banner image with alternative noted.
verses.before: He brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me was love.
verses.after: He brought me into the house of wine; his banner over me was love.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me was love.

verses.rationale: Retain foods and lovesickness as bodily metaphor.
verses.before: Sustain me with raisin cakes; refresh me with apples, for I am sick with love.
verses.after: Sustain me with raisin cakes; refresh me with apples, for I am sick with love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sustain me with raisin cakes; refresh me with apples, for I am sick with love.

verses.rationale: Preserve left/right and actual embrace.
verses.before: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
verses.after: His left hand is beneath my head, and his right arm embraces me.
verses.tsw_comparator: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.

verses.rationale: Keep animal oath, paired verbs, and love’s own timing.
verses.before: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.
verses.after: I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it wishes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.

verses.rationale: Retain exclamation and parallel motion.
verses.before: The voice of my beloved! Look, he comes, leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills.
verses.after: The sound of my beloved! Look, he is coming, leaping over mountains, bounding over hills.
verses.tsw_comparator: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills.

verses.rationale: Keep animal comparison and three spatial details.
verses.before: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, looking through the lattice.
verses.after: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, peering through the lattice.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Behold, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, looking through the lattice.

verses.rationale: Make quotation boundary audible without extra characterization.
verses.before: My beloved answered and said to me, “Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
verses.after: My beloved speaks to me: “Rise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved answered and said to me, “Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.

verses.rationale: Retain doubled departure of rainy season.
verses.before: For look, the winter has passed; the rain is over and gone.
verses.after: Look, winter has passed; the rain is over and gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: For behold, the winter has passed; the rain is over and gone.

verses.rationale: Choose singing with pruning alternative in note.
verses.before: The flowers appear on the earth, the time of singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
verses.after: Flowers appear on the earth; the season of singing has arrived, and the turtledove’s voice is heard in our land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The flowers appear on the earth, the time of singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.

verses.rationale: Preserve seasonal produce and repeated invitation.
verses.before: The fig tree ripens its early figs, and the vines in blossom give forth fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
verses.after: The fig tree is ripening its early fruit; blossoming vines give off their fragrance. Rise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fig tree ripens its early figs, and the vines in blossom give forth fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.

verses.rationale: Retain concealed dove and paired requests.
verses.before: O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
verses.after: My dove in the rock’s clefts, in the hiding place of the steep cliffs, let me see your face, let me hear your voice. Your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.”
verses.tsw_comparator: O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.

verses.rationale: Keep plural command and vineyard vulnerability without decoding symbolism.
verses.before: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards, for our vineyards are in blossom.”
verses.after: Catch us the foxes, the little foxes ruining the vineyards, for our vineyards are in bloom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards, for our vineyards are in blossom.”

verses.rationale: Retain mutual belonging and grazing image.
verses.before: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He pastures his flock among the lilies.
verses.after: My beloved is mine, and I am his; he grazes among the lilies.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He pastures his flock among the lilies.

verses.rationale: Keep day’s breath and uncertain Bether interpretation in note.
verses.before: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the rugged mountains.
verses.after: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved. Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the cleft mountains.
verses.tsw_comparator: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the rugged mountains.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated seeking and plural nights.
verses.before: Upon my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I did not find him.
verses.after: On my bed, night after night, I sought the one my whole being loves. I sought him but did not find him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Upon my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I did not find him.

verses.rationale: Keep resolve, civic spaces, and exact search refrain.
verses.before: “I will arise now and go about the city, in the streets and in the squares. I will seek him whom my soul loves.” I sought him, but I did not find him.
verses.after: “I will get up and go through the city, through its streets and squares, to seek the one my whole being loves.” I sought him but did not find him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will arise now and go about the city, in the streets and in the squares. I will seek him whom my soul loves.” I sought him, but I did not find him.

verses.rationale: Preserve reversal from seeking to being found.
verses.before: The watchmen found me as they went about in the city. “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
verses.after: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. “Have you seen the one my whole being loves?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The watchmen found me as they went about in the city. “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”

verses.rationale: Retain active woman and maternal room specificity.
verses.before: Scarcely had I passed them when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him and would not let him go until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her who conceived me.
verses.after: Scarcely had I passed them when I found the one my whole being loves. I held him and would not let him go until I brought him to my mother’s house, to the room of the woman who conceived me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Scarcely had I passed them when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him and would not let him go until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her who conceived me.

verses.rationale: Match repeated oath exactly.
verses.before: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.
verses.after: I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it wishes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.

verses.rationale: Keep question and procession’s scented imagery.
verses.before: What is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all the fragrant powders of a merchant?
verses.after: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, fragrant with myrrh and frankincense, with all the merchant’s scented powders?
verses.tsw_comparator: What is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all the fragrant powders of a merchant?

verses.rationale: Retain sixty and Israel repetition.
verses.before: Look, it is Solomon's couch. Sixty mighty men surround it, of the mighty men of Israel,
verses.after: Look! Solomon’s litter! Sixty warriors surround it, warriors of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, it is Solomon's couch. Sixty mighty men surround it, of the mighty men of Israel,

verses.rationale: Preserve martial protection and night fears.
verses.before: all of them bearing swords and trained in war, each with his sword at his side, because of fear in the night.
verses.after: All of them grip the sword, trained for battle, each with his sword at his thigh against the terrors of the night.
verses.tsw_comparator: all of them bearing swords and trained in war, each with his sword at his side, because of fear in the night.

verses.rationale: Keep named king, carriage, and wood source.
verses.before: King Solomon made for himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon.
verses.after: King Solomon made himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon made for himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon.

verses.rationale: Preserve unusual love-inlay wording with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: He made its posts of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple. Its interior was inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.after: He made its posts of silver, its support of gold, its seat of purple cloth, its interior inlaid with love from the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made its posts of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple. Its interior was inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retain Zion address, mother, and doubled day.
verses.before: Go out, O daughters of Zion, and look upon King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, on the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.after: Come out, daughters of Zion, and look at King Solomon wearing the crown his mother gave him on his wedding day, the day his heart rejoiced.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go out, O daughters of Zion, and look upon King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, on the day of the gladness of his heart.

verses.rationale: Keep refrain, veil, and moving goat image.
verses.before: Look, you are beautiful, my love; look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down the slopes of Gilead.
verses.after: How beautiful you are, my love! How beautiful! Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, you are beautiful, my love; behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down the slopes of Gilead.

verses.rationale: Retain twin/bereaved imagery rather than explain matching teeth.
verses.before: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes that have come up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and none among them has lost its young.
verses.after: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn sheep coming up from washing, each bearing twins, none bereaved among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes that have come up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and none among them has lost its young.

verses.rationale: Keep thread, color, fruit, and veil.
verses.before: Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks are like halves of a pomegranate behind your veil.
verses.after: Your lips are a scarlet thread; your mouth is lovely. Your temples are slices of pomegranate behind your veil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks are like halves of a pomegranate behind your veil.

verses.rationale: Keep thousand and uncertain construction term in note.
verses.before: Your neck is like the tower of David, built in rows of stone. Upon it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
verses.after: Your neck is like David’s tower, built in courses; a thousand shields hang on it, all the shields of warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your neck is like the tower of David, built in rows of stone. Upon it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.

verses.rationale: Retain breasts and doubled two image without euphemism.
verses.before: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, that pasture among the lilies.
verses.after: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among the lilies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, that pasture among the lilies.

verses.rationale: Match day phrase and preserve aromatic landscape.
verses.before: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
verses.after: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.
verses.tsw_comparator: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

verses.rationale: Retain whole-person praise without theological import.
verses.before: You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no blemish in you.
verses.after: You are beautiful in every part, my love; there is no blemish in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no blemish in you.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated invitation, three named heights, predators.
verses.before: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride; come with me from Lebanon. Depart from the summit of Amana, from the summit of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
verses.after: Come with me from Lebanon, bride; come with me from Lebanon. Look down from Amana’s summit, from the peaks of Senir and Hermon, from lions’ dens, from mountains of leopards.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride; come with me from Lebanon. Depart from the summit of Amana, from the summit of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.

verses.rationale: Preserve doubled heart capture and sister/bride endearment.
verses.before: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have captured my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
verses.after: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have captured my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have captured my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated kin/endearment and sensory comparisons.
verses.before: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your oils than any spice.
verses.after: How lovely your caresses, my sister, my bride! How much better than wine! The fragrance of your oils surpasses every spice.
verses.tsw_comparator: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your oils than any spice.

verses.rationale: Retain tactile and geographic scents.
verses.before: Your lips drip nectar, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
verses.after: Your lips drip nectar, bride; honey and milk are beneath your tongue. Your clothes smell like Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your lips drip nectar, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.

verses.rationale: Preserve enclosed garden and two water sources; note gal uncertainty.
verses.before: A garden locked is my sister, my bride, a spring locked, a fountain sealed.
verses.after: A locked garden is my sister, my bride, a locked spring, a sealed fountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: A garden locked is my sister, my bride, a spring locked, a fountain sealed.

verses.rationale: Keep garden catalogue beginning across verse boundary.
verses.before: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates with choice fruits, henna with nard,
verses.after: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates with choice fruits, henna with nard,
verses.tsw_comparator: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates with choice fruits, henna with nard,

verses.rationale: Retain repeated nard and full aromatic list.
verses.before: nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
verses.after: nard and saffron, sweet cane and cinnamon, with every frankincense tree, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
verses.tsw_comparator: nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.

verses.rationale: Preserve living water and mountain source.
verses.before: A garden fountain, a well of living water, and flowing streams from Lebanon.
verses.after: You are a garden fountain, a well of living water, streams flowing from Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: A garden fountain, a well of living water, and flowing streams from Lebanon.

verses.rationale: Retain woman’s invitation and my/his garden shift.
verses.before: Awake, north wind, and come, south wind. Blow upon my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choicest fruits.
verses.after: Wake, north wind! Come, south wind! Blow through my garden; let its spices flow. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choice fruits.
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, north wind, and come, south wind. Blow upon my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choicest fruits.

verses.rationale: Keep completed first-person actions and plural invitation without assigning new speaker dogmatically.
verses.before: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey. I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends; drink, and be drunk with love.
verses.after: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice, eaten my honeycomb with my honey, drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends! Drink deeply, lovers!
verses.tsw_comparator: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey. I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends; drink, and be drunk with love.

verses.rationale: Retain waking/dream tension and four endearments.
verses.before: I slept, but my heart was awake. The sound of my beloved! He is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is wet with dew, my locks with the drops of the night.”
verses.after: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. The sound of my beloved knocking! “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the drops of night.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I slept, but my heart was awake. The sound of my beloved! He is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is wet with dew, my locks with the drops of the night.”

verses.rationale: Preserve doubled reluctance questions.
verses.before: I had taken off my robe; must I put it on again? I had washed my feet; must I soil them again?
verses.after: “I have taken off my tunic— how can I put it on again? I have washed my feet— how can I dirty them?”
verses.tsw_comparator: I had taken off my robe; must I put it on again? I had washed my feet; must I soil them again?

verses.rationale: Keep opening and bodily arousal without overexplaining.
verses.before: My beloved put his hand to the latch, and my heart was stirred within me.
verses.after: My beloved reached his hand through the opening, and my inward parts stirred for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved put his hand to the latch, and my heart was stirred within me.

verses.rationale: Preserve perfume and door mechanism.
verses.before: I arose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, upon the handles of the bolt.
verses.after: I rose to open to my beloved. My hands dripped myrrh, my fingers flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
verses.tsw_comparator: I arose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, upon the handles of the bolt.

verses.rationale: Retain difficult when-he-spoke chronology and failed search.
verses.before: I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone. My soul failed me when he spoke. I sought him, but I did not find him. I called him, but he gave no answer.
verses.after: I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had slipped away, gone. My very life went out when he spoke. I sought him but did not find him; I called, but he did not answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone. My soul failed me when he spoke. I sought him, but I did not find him. I called him, but he gave no answer.

verses.rationale: Keep assault explicit and distinguish no imagined rescue.
verses.before: The watchmen found me as they went about in the city. They struck me; they wounded me. The keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
verses.after: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. They struck me; they wounded me. The guards of the walls took my wrap from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The watchmen found me as they went about in the city. They struck me; they wounded me. The keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

verses.rationale: Retain question-and-answer oath form.
verses.before: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, what will you tell him? Tell him that I am sick with love.
verses.after: I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem: if you find my beloved, what will you tell him? That I am sick with love.
verses.tsw_comparator: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, what will you tell him? Tell him that I am sick with love.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated challenge and female address.
verses.before: What is your beloved more than another beloved, O most beautiful among women? What is your beloved more than another beloved, that you so adjure us?
verses.after: How is your beloved more than another beloved, most beautiful of women? How is your beloved more than another beloved, that you put us under such an oath?
verses.tsw_comparator: What is your beloved more than another beloved, O most beautiful among women? What is your beloved more than another beloved, that you so adjure us?

verses.rationale: Keep complexion imagery and exact number.
verses.before: My beloved is radiant and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand.
verses.after: My beloved is radiant and ruddy, standing out among ten thousand.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved is radiant and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand.

verses.rationale: Retain mixed precious-metal and living color images.
verses.before: His head is finest gold; his locks are wavy, black as a raven.
verses.after: His head is finest gold; his hair falls in curls, black as a raven.
verses.tsw_comparator: His head is finest gold; his locks are wavy, black as a raven.

verses.rationale: Make the obscure fullness-setting phrase readable as securely fitted eyes; retain dove and milk images and note uncertainty.
verses.before: His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, washed with milk, set beside fullness.
verses.after: His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, bathed in milk, securely set.
verses.tsw_comparator: His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, washed with milk, set beside fullness.

verses.rationale: Retain garden, lips, and liquid perfume.
verses.before: His cheeks are like beds of spices, mounds of sweet-scented herbs. His lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh.
verses.after: His cheeks are beds of spice, mounds of fragrant herbs. His lips are lilies dripping flowing myrrh.
verses.tsw_comparator: His cheeks are like beds of spices, mounds of sweet-scented herbs. His lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh.

verses.rationale: Preserve bodily jewel imagery, note ancient stone uncertainty.
verses.before: His arms are rods of gold, set with jewels. His body is polished ivory, adorned with sapphires.
verses.after: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His abdomen is polished ivory overlaid with sapphires.
verses.tsw_comparator: His arms are rods of gold, set with jewels. His body is polished ivory, adorned with sapphires.

verses.rationale: Keep architecture and landscape as parallel praise.
verses.before: His legs are pillars of marble, set upon bases of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
verses.after: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as its cedars.
verses.tsw_comparator: His legs are pillars of marble, set upon bases of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.

verses.rationale: Preserve desire and friend alongside beloved.
verses.before: His mouth is most sweet, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.after: His mouth is sweetness itself; every part of him is desirable. This is my beloved, this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: His mouth is most sweet, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep plural offer and repeated beloved.
verses.before: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?
verses.after: Where has your beloved gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did your beloved turn? We will seek him with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?

verses.rationale: Retain pastoral/garden ambiguity.
verses.before: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
verses.after: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spice, to graze in the gardens and gather lilies.
verses.tsw_comparator: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.

verses.rationale: Preserve reversed order from2:16 and repeated grazing.
verses.before: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine. He pastures his flock among the lilies.
verses.after: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine; he grazes among the lilies.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine. He pastures his flock among the lilies.

verses.rationale: Keep two cities and military comparison.
verses.before: You are beautiful as Tirzah, my love, lovely as Jerusalem, majestic as an army with banners.
verses.after: You are beautiful as Tirzah, my love, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as troops with banners.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are beautiful as Tirzah, my love, lovely as Jerusalem, majestic as an army with banners.

verses.rationale: Retain power of gaze and repeated goat image with source distinction.
verses.before: Turn your eyes away from me, for they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats leaping down from Gilead.
verses.after: Turn your eyes away from me; they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn your eyes away from me, for they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats leaping down from Gilead.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated twin metaphor but ewes rather than shorn sheep.
verses.before: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes that have come up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and none among them has lost its young.
verses.after: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes coming up from washing, each bearing twins, none bereaved among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes that have come up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and none among them has lost its young.

verses.rationale: Match repeated praise from4:3.
verses.before: Your cheeks are like halves of a pomegranate behind your veil.
verses.after: Your temples are slices of pomegranate behind your veil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your cheeks are like halves of a pomegranate behind your veil.

verses.rationale: Retain exact harem categories and numbers.
verses.before: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and young women without number.
verses.after: There may be sixty queens, eighty concubines, and young women beyond counting,
verses.tsw_comparator: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number.

verses.rationale: Keep unique/only language and women’s praise.
verses.before: But my dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is the only one of her mother, pure to her who bore her. The daughters saw her and called her blessed; the queens and the concubines also, and they praised her:
verses.after: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, her mother’s only one, the cherished one of her who bore her. Young women saw her and called her fortunate; queens and concubines praised her.
verses.tsw_comparator: But my dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is the only one of her mother, pure to her who bore her. The daughters saw her and called her blessed; the queens and the concubines also, and they praised her:

verses.rationale: Retain luminous progression and banner refrain.
verses.before: “Who is this who looks forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, majestic as an army with banners?”
verses.after: “Who is this looking out like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, awesome as troops with banners?”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Who is this who looks forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, majestic as an army with banners?”

verses.rationale: Keep unspecified first-person speaker and botanical inspection.
verses.before: I went down to the nut orchard to look at the blossoms of the valley, to see whether the vines had budded and the pomegranates were in bloom.
verses.after: I went down to the nut orchard to see the valley’s new growth, to see whether the vines had budded and the pomegranates were in bloom.
verses.tsw_comparator: I went down to the nut orchard to look at the blossoms of the valley, to see whether the vines had budded and the pomegranates were in bloom.

verses.rationale: Retain difficult soul/chariots phrase with alternatives in note.
verses.before: Before I knew it, my desire set me among the chariots of my noble people.
verses.after: Before I knew it, my desire had set me among the chariots of my noble people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before I knew it, my desire set me among the chariots of my noble people.

verses.rationale: Map source7:1 to public6:13; retain four returns and question.
verses.before: Return, return, O Shulammite; return, return, that we may gaze upon you. Why should you gaze upon the Shulammite, as upon the dance of Mahanaim?
verses.after: Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, so we may look at you! Why would you look at the Shulammite as at a dance of two camps?
verses.tsw_comparator: Return, return, O Shulammite; return, return, that we may gaze upon you. Why should you gaze upon the Shulammite, as upon the dance of Mahanaim?

verses.rationale: Map source7:2 to public7:1; retain thighs and skilled craft.
verses.before: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O noble daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of an artist.
verses.after: How lovely your steps in sandals, noble daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of a craftsman’s hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O noble daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of an artist.

verses.rationale: Retain bodily and agricultural images without euphemism.
verses.before: Your navel is a rounded bowl that never lacks mixed wine. Your waist is a heap of wheat encircled with lilies.
verses.after: Your navel is a rounded bowl— may it never lack mixed wine. Your belly is a heap of wheat ringed with lilies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your navel is a rounded bowl that never lacks mixed wine. Your waist is a heap of wheat encircled with lilies.

verses.rationale: Preserve shortened recurring simile.
verses.before: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
verses.after: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

verses.rationale: Retain all body parts, places, and viewing direction.
verses.before: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, which looks toward Damascus.
verses.after: Your neck is an ivory tower. Your eyes are pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like Lebanon’s tower looking toward Damascus.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, which looks toward Damascus.

verses.rationale: Keep royal captivity by hair image.
verses.before: Your head crowns you like Carmel, and the flowing locks of your head are like purple. A king is held captive by its tresses.
verses.after: Your head crowns you like Carmel; your flowing hair is like purple cloth. A king is held captive in its tresses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your head crowns you like Carmel, and the flowing locks of your head are like purple. A king is held captive by its tresses.

verses.rationale: Retain address as love and sensuous plural pleasures.
verses.before: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, O love, with all your delights!
verses.after: How beautiful, how delightful you are, love with all your pleasures!
verses.tsw_comparator: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, O love, with all your delights!

verses.rationale: Keep body/tree correspondence.
verses.before: Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters.
verses.after: Your stature is like a palm tree, your breasts like its clusters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters.

verses.rationale: Retain first-person resolve and ensuing wishes.
verses.before: I said, “I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your breath like apples,
verses.after: I said, “I will climb the palm and take hold of its branches.” May your breasts be like clusters of grapes, your breath fragrant as apples,
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, “I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your breath like apples,

verses.rationale: Preserve sudden my-beloved shift, pinned sleepers reading, and wine stirring their lips.
verses.before: and your mouth like the best wine.
verses.after: and your mouth like fine wine— going down smoothly for my beloved, stirring the lips of sleepers.
verses.tsw_comparator: and your mouth like the best wine.

verses.rationale: Keep woman’s declaration and desire directed toward her.
verses.before: I am my beloved's, and his desire is for me.
verses.after: I am my beloved’s, and his desire is for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am my beloved's, and his desire is for me.

verses.rationale: Retain woman’s initiative and rural lodging.
verses.before: Come, my beloved, let us go out into the fields and lodge among the villages.
verses.after: Come, my beloved, let us go out to the fields; let us spend the night in the villages.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come, my beloved, let us go out into the fields and lodge among the villages.

verses.rationale: Keep shared inspection and explicit woman’s gift of affection.
verses.before: Let us go out early to the vineyards and see whether the vines have budded, whether the blossoms have opened, and whether the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.
verses.after: Let us rise early for the vineyards to see whether the vines have budded, whether the blossoms have opened and the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my caresses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us go out early to the vineyards and see whether the vines have budded, whether the blossoms have opened, and whether the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.

verses.rationale: Retain mandrakes, two ages of fruit, and stored gift.
verses.before: The mandrakes give forth fragrance, and beside our doors are all choice fruits, new as well as old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
verses.after: The mandrakes give off their scent, and at our doors are all kinds of choice fruits, new and old, which I have stored for you, my beloved.
verses.tsw_comparator: The mandrakes give forth fragrance, and beside our doors are all choice fruits, new as well as old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.

verses.rationale: Preserve counterfactual brother comparison and public affection’s constraint.
verses.before: Oh that you were like a brother to me, one who nursed at my mother's breasts! Then, if I found you outside, I would kiss you, and none would despise me.
verses.after: If only you were like a brother to me, nursed at my mother’s breasts! Then, finding you outside, I could kiss you, and no one would despise me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh that you were like a brother to me, one who nursed at my mother's breasts! Then, if I found you outside, I would kiss you, and none would despise me.

verses.rationale: Choose mother as teacher with alternative you in note.
verses.before: I would lead you and bring you into my mother's house, she who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranate.
verses.after: I would lead you and bring you to my mother’s house, where she would teach me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranate.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would lead you and bring you into my mother's house, she who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranate.

verses.rationale: Match embrace refrain.
verses.before: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
verses.after: His left hand is beneath my head, and his right arm embraces me.
verses.tsw_comparator: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.

verses.rationale: Retain changed interrogative oath without adding absent animals.
verses.before: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.
verses.after: I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem: why stir up or awaken love before it wishes?
verses.tsw_comparator: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.

verses.rationale: Preserve gender transition and doubled birth memory.
verses.before: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother was in labor with you; there she who bore you was in labor.
verses.after: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you; there your mother labored with you, there she who bore you was in labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother was in labor with you; there she who bore you was in labor.

verses.rationale: Retain jealousy, Sheol, and divided divine-name source with alternative noted.
verses.before: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy is fierce as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, the very flame of the LORD.
verses.after: Set me like a seal on your heart, like a seal on your arm. For love is strong as death, jealousy relentless as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of **YAH**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy is fierce as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, the very flame of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep resistance to flood and unpurchasable love.
verses.before: Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers overwhelm it. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly despised.
verses.after: Many waters cannot extinguish love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man offered all his household wealth for love, he would be utterly scorned.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers overwhelm it. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly despised.

verses.rationale: Preserve family’s question about immature sister without assigning age.
verses.before: We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What will we do for our sister on the day when she is spoken for?
verses.after: We have a little sister, and she has no breasts yet. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
verses.tsw_comparator: We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day when she is spoken for?

verses.rationale: Keep conditional family construction images without interpretive substitution.
verses.before: If she is a wall, we will build upon her a battlement of silver. But if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
verses.after: If she is a wall, we will build a silver turret on her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with a cedar plank.
verses.tsw_comparator: If she is a wall, we will build upon her a battlement of silver. But if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.

verses.rationale: Retain woman’s reply, bodily maturity, and peace word.
verses.before: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. Then I became in his eyes as one who finds peace.
verses.after: I am a wall, and my breasts are towers. Then in his eyes I became like one who finds peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. Then I became in his eyes as one who finds peace.

verses.rationale: Preserve owner, place, entrusted cultivation, and amount.
verses.before: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He entrusted the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring for its fruit a thousand pieces of silver.
verses.after: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He entrusted it to keepers; each was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He entrusted the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring for its fruit a thousand pieces of silver.

verses.rationale: Retain emphatic ownership and literal before-me relation without adding a decision to give the vineyard; preserve distinct amounts.
verses.before: My vineyard, my own, is before me. You, O Solomon, may have the thousand, and the keepers of its fruit two hundred.
verses.after: My vineyard, my own, is in my keeping. The thousand are yours, Solomon, and two hundred for those who keep its fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: My vineyard, my own, is before me. You, O Solomon, may have the thousand, and the keepers of its fruit two hundred.

verses.rationale: Retain female addressee and singular request among listeners.
verses.before: O you who dwell in the gardens, the companions listen for your voice; let me hear it.
verses.after: You who dwell in the gardens, companions are listening for your voice. Let me hear it!
verses.tsw_comparator: O you who dwell in the gardens, the companions listen for your voice; let me hear it.

verses.rationale: Keep imperative escape and recurring gazelle imagery at open ending.
verses.before: Hurry, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the mountains of spices.
verses.after: Hurry away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hurry, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the mountains of spices.

comparative_references.scope: All 117 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
